answer: Coordination-priced admission charging for pairwise links. Each new agent must post a yarrow-token deposit for every distinct counterparty it transacts with, and the deposit locks proportionally to how many existing agents that counterparty already touches. An attacker creating many identities must pay rising jade-denominated fees per link as overlap grows, since each shared neighbor multiplies the required escrow. Fake clusters therefore cost superlinearly in ivory-weighted collateral, while honest single-link agents pay near the base rate.
